key_insight: A spring-loaded probe can extract a liquid ligament from a bath and tune it into a reliable single-drop generator by balancing probe radius and retraction length.
engineering_relevance: This offers a simple, repeatable way to produce uniform droplets or ordered droplet arrays for lab microfluidics and pilot-wave experiments, including on vibrating baths.
method: Vary probe radius a and retraction length L to control ligament stretching.
Use the intermediate regime for single-drop formation; too little stretch gives no drop, too much gives multiple drops.
Leverage the scaling R ~ a^(2/3) L^(1/3) to predict drop size from geometry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three distinct regimes and repeatable single-droplet production with less than 5% variation in drop radius.
watch_item: Performance depends on precise tuning of a and L; moving outside the narrow single-drop regime can suppress drops or create multiple drops.
paper_title: Controlled drop generation via ligament extraction from a static or vibrating liquid bath
